disposition_reason: Tables 4-6 print statistics for 23 elements (including Cd, Pb, Hg) in ciders, flavored beer-based low-alcohol beverages and their pooled set.

study.design: Market and home-made survey of ciders and flavored low-alcohol beverages
study.origin: Ciders from Polish producers; beer-based low-percentage beverages from local and international producers; home-made ciders from two apple juices
study.method: Degassing, microwave HNO3 digestion; ICP-MS (Ag, Ba, Bi, Cd, Co, Cr, Li, Mn, Ni, Pb, Sr, Tl), ICP-OES (Al, B, Ca, Cu, Fe, K, Mg, Na, Ti, Zn), CV-AAS (Hg)
study.lod_text: LOD values not printed in the main text
study.qa: Indium internal standard; triplicates; validation details not printed in main text

controls.outcome: Home-made vs commercial median: Ni 188.4 vs 59.60 µg/L; Cu 236.5 vs 44.00 µg/L; Cr 24.71 vs 23.16 µg/L; Na 25.04 vs 112.4 mg/L

controls.control: Glass bottle vs can, one cider brand and batch
controls.outcome: Significant differences for Cu (p=0.036), Mn (p=0.037), Na (p=0.025); Na and Cu higher in bottles, Mn higher in cans; values figure-only or in Supplementary Table S2

regulatory_or_exposure.value: Pb exceeded the 10 µg/L WHO/Polish drinking-water value in 45 cases; Cd exceeded WHO 3 µg/L once; alcoholic-beverage limits for Cd and Pb not exceeded

unresolved: LOD values not printed; Pb below LOD in 19 samples, Hg below LOD in all.
Table 4 pools ciders, beer-based beverages and the two juices; juice-only values not printed.
Table 4 Ba maximum 465.2 µg/L exceeds both Table 5 maxima (211.2 and 460.1 µg/L); Zn maximum 606.0 vs 533.2 in Table 5.
Packaging comparison values are in Supplementary Table S2 (not in filed PDF); figure-only here.
